_note: The clauses the SHIPPED law must state for the mechanisms the kit ships (board #170).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. TEMPLATE/ ships the patrol's receipt legs, the shared field
predicate and their tests, and its law stated NONE of their preconditions: measured
2026-09-28, TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl carried 0 occurrences of `receipt_subject`,
`duty=completed`, `retired_logs` and `named after ITS OWN JOB`, against 1/1/1/2 in the
live law. A factory bootstrapped from the template therefore inherits both legs with
none of the rules that make them work, which is section 11's own clause: a mechanism
whose precondition is undocumented is a permanent silent exclusion.
WHY IT IS NOT A PAIRS ENTRY. `skills/meta-factory/SKILL.md` and
`TEMPLATE/SKILL.md.tmpl` are deliberately NOT byte-paired - they are independent
documents that happen to share a structure, with different section numbering. So no
gate can assert equivalence of the two files, and this file is where 'what the shipped
law must state' is DECLARED instead.
HOW AN ENTRY IS READ. Each entry names the MECHANISM that needs the clause, the TOKEN
the mechanism keys on, and the CLAUSE PHRASE the law must carry. The gate asserts BOTH
sides: the token is present in the shipped mechanism's own source (so a declaration
cannot go stale when the mechanism changes) and the clause phrase is present in the
shipped law (so a mechanism cannot ship with its precondition unstated).
A CLAUSE IS NAMED BY ITS PHRASE, NEVER BY A SECTION NUMBER. The two law files number
their sections differently - this factory's section 11 is State, the template's is
Escalation - so a section number resolves to a DIFFERENT clause in each tree (#184,
ruled on the kit's own citation law).
WHY `law` IS A LIST (board #302). The clause tail of the template's law body was
extracted into `TEMPLATE/state.md.tmpl` (the State section's clause tail) and
`TEMPLATE/verdicts-and-claims.md.tmpl` (the Verdicts section), so the shipped law is
no longer ONE file. The gate asserts each clause phrase against the CONCATENATION of
the named files, so a clause reads as 'stated by the shipped law' wherever the shipped
law carries it - and a named file that is absent or empty is still a failure.

required_clauses.clause: A duty receipt is DECLARED, and the declaration is one whole line
required_clauses.why: RECEIPT_DECL_RE (patrol_host_state.py) reads the anchored line `receipt_subject: <stem>` on the row. Without the clause stating that the declaration is one whole line on its own, a member reads a row that omits it as a duty that owed nothing, and the leg passes by silence.

required_clauses.clause: The receipt's SUBJECT is canonical, and the reader's key is deliberately NOT widened
required_clauses.why: receipt_subject_matches() keys on the boundary-checked prefix `<stem>-<round>`. Without the clause stating the subject form and refusing the fuzzy match, a member widens the key to meet a deviation and the leg reports a false CLEAN, which is the failure it cannot see (#160).

required_clauses.clause: A subject match is not a receipt — the row must DECLARE its completion
required_clauses.why: The leg reads `duty=completed|failed|skipped` through declared_duty() against DUTY_DOMAIN. Without the clause, a DISPATCH record written before the round completed certifies it, and a round with no receipt at all reads clean.

required_clauses.clause: A pacemaker's redirect log is named after ITS OWN JOB
required_clauses.why: NOTIFY_LOG_RE takes the log filename's stem as a cron job NAME and looks it up among the rows the factory declares. That makes `the redirect label equals the job name` a load-bearing contract between every pacemaker prompt and the leg; unwritten, one job carried a hand-typed label for 16 rounds and every log landed in retired_logs as history, never judged (#163).

The clause states that a job declaring no stem is NOT JUDGED and is counted and named so its silence is visible, and that the declaration is an ATTRIBUTION KEY rather than a claim that nothing else records the work. Without it a member reads a NOT JUDGED row as a pass.

required_clauses.clause: A dispatch notify names the unit it routes in its opening non-blank line
required_clauses.why: dispatch_delivery_leg reads a delivery's header through delivery_header(), whose scan is bounded by DELIVERY_HEADER_LINES = 1: it keys on the ONE line a delivery DECLARES itself on, measured from the #433 specimen's discriminator and deliberately NOT widened (widening it re-opened #433). That makes `the unit is named in the opening non-blank line` a load-bearing contract between every dispatch notify and the leg, and it was stated nowhere: the mechanism ships into every kit (TEMPLATE/tools/patrol_host_state.py is byte-identical to root) while its precondition was undocumented - the #170 class. A dispatch that names its subject only in the body is invisible to the leg, which is the reader-side defect #433 fixed and this is its writer-side twin.
